name: Elaine Luria
subject: Chutzpah
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR AND AUTHORIZED BY SCHIFF FOR SENATE
body:
|
[](https://act.adamschiff.com/go/1014?c0=abs_em_luria.tkB0OZ&refcode=AU_ABS_FR_TAN_GEN_AC90_20251113_PM1_V1_S1&t=3&akid=9183%2E5257348%2EOYThGc)
Derek, it’s Elaine Luria and Adam said I could reach out.
_Chutzpah_ — is a Yiddish term that means _guts_ or _courage_.
In 1906, my great-grandfather left his home in Poland, made the long journey through Europe and across the Atlantic, and landed in Jasper, Alabama.
That took some serious _chutzpah_.
My great-grandfather believed so strongly in the promise of America – a place where he could be Jewish without fear, where he could forge his own path – that he left his whole world behind.
That promise came true for him. He built a life, a family, and a proud community.
That’s what sets America apart, Derek. Here, anyone with a little _chutzpah_ is free to be whoever they want to be, do whatever they want to do, and achieve more than they ever dreamed.
In 1993, I joined the Navy to defend those freedoms.
In 2018, I ran for Congress to expand them.
In 2020, I won re-election to continue that work, making our nation free, safe, and prosperous.
In 2022, I served on the January 6th Committee because our Constitutional freedoms were threatened.
In 2026, I’m running for Congress again, because our current representative either can’t or _won’t_ protect them.
The fact is that Coastal Virginia is in crisis. Our community’s been hit hard by this president’s failed agenda. **It’s time for action.**
Flipping Virginia’s Second District won’t be easy. Dark money groups and super PACs are watching closely, trying to see if we’re strong enough to pose a real threat. **This will be one of the toughest fights of the 2026 election cycle.**
Luckily, _chutzpah_ runs in my family. I’m not afraid of a little _mishigas_. And with you behind me, I’m ready to be the unapologetic champion Virginia families need.
**[Will you become a Founding Donor by splitting a donation of $25 or more between my campaign and Adam Schiff to help me win this battleground race and restore America’s promise for ALL?](https://act.adamschiff.com/go/1370?c0=abs_em_luria.Brh7W-&refcode=AU_ABS_FR_TAN_GEN_AC90_20251113_PM1_V1_S1&t=4&akid=9183%2E5257348%2EOYThGc)**

body:
[1]Justice Democrats

Peter,

Last week, we called for a primary challenge against Senator Chuck
Schumer. Now, people from across the country are joining us in saying
Schumer has got to GO.

Time and again, Schumer has caved to Donald Trump, far-right Republicans,
and corporate interests when it matters most. Last week’s shutdown deal
was just the latest in a long line of capitulations under his leadership.

As Minority Leader, his job is to unite the Democratic caucus as the
opposition party and stand up to Trump’s agenda. But instead, he let 8
Democratic Senators defect and vote to let Republicans gut our health care
— including his own second-in-command in leadership, Whip Sen. Dick
Durbin.

This is a moment of real momentum. More and more people are waking up to
the FAILURE of Democratic leadership in Congress and realizing it’s time
to #DumpChuck. We can’t waste it.

That’s why we’re joining progressives across the country to demand that
Schumer resign, so he can be replaced with an appointee by the governor
ASAP. The working-class people of New York and the country at large
deserve a leader who will actually fight for them—not cave at the most
critical moment.

| | Dorian Gray glanced at the picture, and suddenly an uncontrollable feeling of hatred for Basil Hallward came over him, as though it had been suggested to him by the image on the canvas, whispered into his ear by those grinning lips. The mad passions of a hunted animal stirred within him, and he loathed the man who was seated at the table, more than in his whole life he had ever loathed anything. He glanced wildly around. Something glimmered on the top of the painted chest that faced him. His eye fell on it. He knew what it was. It was a knife that he had brought up, some days before, to cut a piece of cord, and had forgotten to take away with him. He moved slowly towards it, passing Hallward as he did so. As soon as he got behind him, he seized it and turned round. Hallward stirred in his chair as if he was going to rise. He rushed at him and dug the knife into the great vein that is behind the ear, crushing the man’s head down on the table and stabbing again and again. There was a stifled groan and the horrible sound of some one choking with blood. Three times the outstretched arms shot up convulsively, waving grotesque, stiff-fingered hands in the air. He stabbed him twice more, but the man did not move. Something began to trickle on the floor. He waited for a moment, still pressing the head down. Then he threw the knife on the table, and listened. He could hear nothing, but the drip, drip on the threadbare carpet. He opened the door and went out on the landing. The house was absolutely quiet. No one was about. For a few seconds he stood bending over the balustrade and peering down into the black seething well of darkness. Then he took out the key and returned to the room, locking himself in as he did so. The thing was still seated in the chair, straining over the table with bowed head, and humped back, and long fantastic arms. Had it not been for the red jagged tear in the neck and the clotted black pool that was slowly widening on the table, one would have said that the man was simply asleep. How quickly it had all been done! He felt strangely calm, and walking over to the window, opened it and stepped out on the balcony. The wind had blown the fog away, and the sky was like a monstrous peacock’s tail, starred with myriads of golden eyes. He looked down and saw the policeman going his rounds and flashing the long beam of his lantern on the doors of the silent houses. The crimson spot of a prowling hansom gleamed at the corner and then vanished. A woman in a fluttering shawl was creeping slowly by the railings, staggering as she went. Now and then she stopped and peered back. Once, she began to sing in a hoarse voice. The policeman strolled over and said something to her. She stumbled away, laughing. A bitter blast swept across the square. The gas-lamps flickered and became blue, and the leafless trees shook their black iron branches to and fro. He shivered and went back, closing the window behind him.

Ivan Dmytrovych Sirko was born in the early seventeenth century, approximately between 1605 and 1610. This is evidenced primarily by the results of research on Sirko's remains, according to which the Cossack ataman was 70-75 years old at the time of his death in 1680. The first researcher of Sirko's biography, the famous Ukrainian historian Dmytro Yavornytskyi, suggested that the future ataman was born in Sloboda Ukraine in the settlement of Merefa (now the city of Merefa, Kharkiv region). However, this is not true. Merefa was founded only in 1658, i.e. when Sirko was in his late teens. However, Sirko and his family lived in Merefa for a long time in his house, and after his death, his wife and some family members lived there. The fact that Merefa in Slobozhanshchyna is associated with the name of the Cossack Ataman is evidenced by another name for the town recorded in some Ukrainian chronicles, Sirkivka. Where, then, should we look for Sirko's homeland? In our opinion, the sources give grounds to localize it in Eastern Podillia, namely in the Vinnytsia region. It is worth recalling that Sirko was a colonel in Vinnytsia (Kalnytsia) in 1658-1660. As you know, at that time in Ukraine, people who came from the local area were usually elected to such positions. Let us also recall a letter from Hetman of the Left Bank Ukraine Ivan Samoilovych to the tsarist voivode Prince G. Romodanovsky of April 20, 1675*, which recounts (in Russian) Sirko's own words: "And since I was born among the Poles, I want to die there." Thus, it is clear that Sirko was born on the Ukrainian lands that were under the rule of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, not Muscovy (the latter included Slobozhanshchyna). The historian Volodymyr Borysenko's assumption that Sirko's birthplace was the hundred-man town of the Bratslav regiment Murafa, a few kilometers from Kalnyk, is correct. Now it is the village of Zhdanov, Vinnytsia region. By the way, Murafa in the Slobozhanshchyna probably originated from this Murafa, because immigrants from the Right Bank of Ukraine to the Left Bank often gave the newly founded settlements the names of their native villages or towns. It is also worth noting Sirko's great interest in Keleberda, which he founded in 1675 on the left bank of the Dnipro. For a long time, he sought from the Moscow tsar the right to own this town or sloboda, as well as the strategically important crossing of the Dnipro near Perevolochna (Sirko wanted this crossing not for himself, but for the entire Zaporozhian Lowland Army). Contrary to popular belief, we believe that Sirko did not come from a Cossack family, but from a small Ukrainian Orthodox gentry. For example, we know the name of a Podillia nobleman, Voytekh Sirko, who was married to a certain Olena Kozynska. Sources mention them in 1592. It is possible that they were relatives of the Cossack leader. Perhaps it is no coincidence that the kings of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, writing to Sirko, called him "urodzon." The word "nobleman" evokes negative associations for many people due to stereotypes instilled in school textbooks of the Stalinist era. However, this approach is not always correct. The term "nobleman" is identical to the words "knight," "chevalier," "nobleman," etc. and was commonly used not only in Poland but also in Ukraine, Belarus, and the Czech Republic. If scholars in Russia, Poland, and the Czech Republic, having contracted vulgar sociologism, no longer accuse Pushkin or Bunin, Suvorov or Kutuzov, Žižka or Kostiushko of being of noble or gentry origin, why have attacks on the Ukrainian and Belarusian gentry continued until recently? Is it not because in this way the imperial "divide and conquer" was transferred to our long-suffering history? Was it not because it was necessary to impose a nihilistic attitude toward the history of Ukraine, to "prove" that Ukrainians or Belarusians were just dark labor without national consciousness, ethnographic material doomed to build other people's empires? Meanwhile, the Ukrainian gentry produced many outstanding sons of Ukraine, fighters for its freedom. Suffice it to mention the names of Kryshtof Kosinski, Petro Konashevych-Sahaidachny, Ivan Sulyma, Ivan Mazepa, Bohdan Khmelnytsky, and his associates: Ivan and Danylo Vyhovsky, Ivan Bohun, Danylo and Ivan Nechai, Mykhailo Krychevsky, Jan Sokolovsky, Siluyan Muzhylovsky, and others. Sirko's appearance and personality do not always coincide with the conventional ideas about him that have developed in some works of art. The Cossack leader was slightly taller than average (174-176 cm), had regular facial features, and a straight nose. By the way, the great Relin intuitively caught this when he depicted him in the center of his painting "Cossacks Writing a Letter to the Turkish Sultan." It is interesting that the prototype for Sirko's image in the painting was the famous military leader General Dragomirov. Only one significant detail was not known to Repin and his consultant D. Yavornytskyi - a red birthmark on Sirko's lower lip on the right side. His contemporaries considered it a "sign of God" given to distinguish him from ordinary people. The Grand Hetman of the Crown, the future King of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, Jan Sobieski, who knew Sirko well and met him in Bratslav in 1671.

As soon as he got behind him, he seized it and turned round. Hallward stirred in his chair as if he was going to rise. He stabbed him twice more, but the man did not move. Something began to trickle on the floor. He waited for a moment, still pressing the head down. Then he threw the knife on the table, and listened. He could hear nothing, but the drip, drip on the threadbare carpet. He opened the door and went out on the landing. The house was absolutely quiet. No one was about. This is evidenced primarily by the results of research on Sirko's remains, according to which the Cossack ataman was 70-75 years old at the time of his death in 1680. The first researcher of Sirko's biography, the famous Ukrainian historian Dmytro Yavornytskyi, suggested that the future ataman was born in Sloboda Ukraine in the settlement of Merefa (now the city of Merefa, Kharkiv region). However, this is not true. Merefa was founded only in 1658, i.e. when Sirko was in his late teens. However, Sirko and his family lived in Merefa for a long time in his house, and after his death, his wife and some family members lived there. The fact that Merefa in Slobozhanshchyna is associated with the name of the Cossack Ataman is evidenced by another name for the town recorded in some Ukrainian chronicles, Sirkivka. Where, then, should we look for Sirko's homeland? In our opinion, the sources give grounds to localize it in Eastern Podillia, namely in the Vinnytsia region. It is worth recalling that Sirko was a colonel in Vinnytsia (Kalnytsia) in 1658-1660. As you know, at that time in Ukraine, people who came from the local area were usually elected to such positions. Let us also recall a letter from Hetman of the Left Bank Ukraine Ivan Samoilovych to the tsarist voivode Prince G. Romodanovsky of April 20, 1675*, which recounts (in Russian) Sirko's own words: "And since I was born among the Poles, I want to die there." Thus, it is clear that Sirko was born on the Ukrainian lands that were under the rule of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, not Muscovy (the latter included Slobozhanshchyna). The historian Volodymyr Borysenko's assumption that Sirko's birthplace was the hundred-man town of the Bratslav regiment Murafa, a few kilometers from Kalnyk, is correct. Now it is the village of Zhdanov, Vinnytsia region. By the way, Murafa in the Slobozhanshchyna probably originated from this Murafa, because immigrants from the Right Bank of Ukraine to the Left Bank often gave the newly founded settlements the names of their native villages or towns. It is also worth noting Sirko's great interest in Keleberda, which he founded in 1675 on the left bank of the Dnipro. For a long time, he sought from the Moscow tsar the right to own this town or sloboda, as well as the strategically important crossing of the Dnipro near Perevolochna (Sirko wanted this crossing not for himself, but for the entire Zaporozhian Lowland Army). Contrary to popular belief, we believe that Sirko did not come from a Cossack family, but from a small Ukrainian Orthodox gentry. For example, we know the name of a Podillia nobleman, Voytekh Sirko, who was married to a certain Olena Kozynska. Sources mention them in 1592. It is possible that they were relatives of the Cossack leader. Perhaps it is no coincidence that the kings of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, writing to Sirko, called him "urodzon." The word "nobleman" evokes negative associations for many people due to stereotypes instilled in school textbooks of the Stalinist era. However, this approach is not always correct. The term "nobleman" is identical to the words "knight," "chevalier," "nobleman," etc. and was commonly used not only in Poland but also in Ukraine, Belarus, and the Czech Republic. If scholars in Russia, Poland, and the Czech Republic, having contracted vulgar sociologism, no longer accuse Pushkin or Bunin, Suvorov or Kutuzov, Žižka or Kostiushko of being of noble or gentry origin, why have attacks on the Ukrainian and Belarusian gentry continued until recently? Is it not because in this way the imperial "divide and conquer" was transferred to our long-suffering history? Was it not because it was necessary to impose a nihilistic attitude toward the history of Ukraine, to "prove" that Ukrainians or Belarusians were just dark labor without national consciousness, ethnographic material doomed to build other people's empires? Meanwhile, the Ukrainian gentry produced many outstanding sons of Ukraine, fighters for its freedom. Suffice it to mention the names of Kryshtof Kosinski, Petro Konashevych-Sahaidachny, Ivan Sulyma, Ivan Mazepa, Bohdan Khmelnytsky, and his associates: Ivan and Danylo Vyhovsky, Ivan Bohun, Danylo and Ivan Nechai, Mykhailo Krychevsky, Jan Sokolovsky, Siluyan Muzhylovsky, and others. Sirko's appearance and personality do not always coincide with the conventional ideas about him that have developed in some works of art. The Cossack leader was slightly taller than average (174-176 cm), had regular facial features, and a straight nose. By the way, the great Relin intuitively caught this when he depicted him in the center of his painting "Cossacks Writing a Letter to the Turkish Sultan." It is interesting that the prototype for Sirko's image in the painting was the famous military leader General Dragomirov. Only one significant detail was not known to Repin and his consultant D. Yavornytskyi - a red birthmark on Sirko's lower lip on the right side. His contemporaries considered it a "sign of God" given to distinguish him from ordinary people. Peter,
When MAGA wants to take credit for something good, they call it the "Trump Effect." In reality, it is actually the "Trump Slump" \- and it is causing grave harm to the people of my district.
People are losing their jobs. Independent sources estimate that in October alone, the country lost 50,000 jobs. Growth has been negative since the moment Trump took over.
Farmers have lost once-competitive markets for products like soybeans, corn, wheat, and beef to China and Argentina (the latter country Trump just gave a $40 billion bailout 👀).
Trump's (likely illegal) tariffs are raising prices for everyone and ruining small businesses.
The Trump Slump is hurting cattle ranchers, small businesses, and farms right here in Eastern Colorado -- and our MAGA rubber stamp representative Lauren Boebert couldn't care less.
Everyone knows that Boebert has got to go. But here's how we will actually beat Lauren Boebert this election:

* This grassroots campaign outraised Boebert 5-1 last quarter, and our war chest dwarfs Boebert's nearly-empty account
* In 2024, we had a record showing for Democrats in this district, overperforming Harris by 6 points while Boebert massively underperformed Trump
* This time, Boebert won't have Trump on the ballot boosting MAGA turnout
* Boebert is only in Congress because of 546 votes

Friend,

I’m in Congress to do right by California’s 45th District -- so when the House passed a spending bill last night that doesn’t address our community’s urgent needs, I was extremely disappointed.

**I voted against the bill because it did _nothing_ to secure affordable healthcare for the thousands of Californians who are seeing their premiums skyrocket.**

And while I cosponsored several amendments to the bill to ensure action on healthcare, Republican leadership refused to even consider them before the vote.

Trump and Congressional Republicans have lied time and again. We can’t trust them to put an extension of the ACA subsidies to a vote -- not while they continue to sell working families out to give their billionaire donors a tax break or spend millions on a lavish, taxpayer-funded ballroom.

That’s what makes flipping the House so important next year. Republicans have shown us their true colors -- and the American people can’t afford to suffer under their leadership any longer. We must retain this seat and flip the House next year.

#
Last year, thanks to this movement, we gave out over 600 turkeys to families at Thanksgiving who didn’t have one. **This year, we hope to double that number.**
[Thanksgiving is two weeks away. Will you chip in $5 or anything you can today to help us bring the joy of the holiday season into homes around NYC this year?](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20251113-turkeys.Pzqoms&refcode=em20251113-10203-P_FND_EGR_GRM&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1&akid=10203%2E2526796%2EujQZiD)

We’re teaming up with NYC public housing developments, community organizations, houses of worship, food pantries and local elected officials to **give hundreds of families an opportunity to celebrate community, mutual aid, and gratitude.**
Many of the organizations we partner with to distribute turkeys — such as the Youth Ministries for Peace & Justice and Glebe Senior Houses — focus on uplifting our most vulnerable communities, including working families on SNAP assistance, asylum seekers new to the U.S., and senior citizens.
We’ve run the numbers, and $15-$20 means a family without a turkey gets to share in the Thanksgiving season.
[Can you chip in $15 — or anything you can today — to help us make that happen?](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20251113-turkeys.Pzqoms&refcode=em20251113-10203-P_FND_EGR_GRM&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=4&akid=10203%2E2526796%2EujQZiD)

From all of us here, thank you for your support.
In solidarity,
Team AOC

There’s no one solution for making homes more affordable. That’s why our plan is multifaceted, covering everything from renting to buying to regulatory processes. These are just three of our key points:
**🏡 Protecting renters.** As your attorney general, I’ve gone after corporate landlords that illegally colluded, used false advertising, and charged "junk" fees to keep rents high and take advantage of tenants. As governor, I’ll continue to fight for renters. In fact, one of our goals is to _materially decrease costs for 100,000 renters by 2035._
**🏡 Assisting first-time home buyers.** Building new housing is important, and we can’t stop there. We need to do more. My administration will work to increase the attainable owner-occupied housing supply by 40,000 units. We’ll expand existing down payment assistance for first-time home buyers. And we’ll push to create new financing tools — especially for people in jobs like teachers, nurses, first responders, and childcare workers.
**🏡 Accelerating permits and cutting red tape.** We can do better than construction delays and higher costs for home buyers. I’ll partner with local governments to get housing development approval times up to best-in-country speeds. And I’ll push to reform all our state housing processes into one streamlined, user-friendly structure that _anyone_ can navigate.

**No fear. No silence.**

body:
We all deserve a Democratic Party that doesn’t back down.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20251113-1&t=1&akid=2833%2E587540%2EtIiweJ)
Hey Peter, it's David.
After years of delays and cover-ups, we might actually see the Epstein files made public.
**That’s because young leaders like Congressman Robert Garcia from California refused to let this issue die.**
He’s under 50, he’s leading the Oversight Committee, and he’s been relentless. He’s been demanding answers, standing up to Republicans, and now — _finally_ — we’re seeing action.
Just yesterday Rep. Adelita Grijalva was sworn in despite Speaker Mike Johnson’s attempts to delay her. Her first move? Signing the discharge petition to release the Epstein files. That means we’re just a week away from real accountability: who Epstein trafficked kids to, and who in power helped cover it up.
Compare that with the eight Senate Democrats (nearly all of whom are retiring) who just caved on the government shutdown, handing a victory to Republicans instead of continuing to fight. If anyone should have been worried about the vulnerability of their seat and voted with Republicans, it should have been someone like Ossoff in Georgia or Gallego in Arizona (both younger senators), but they still did not vote to cave to the Republicans and who did? Eight Senators who have been there for decades and have all the experience in the world, but none of the courage to make it matter. Experience matters, but it means NOTHING if you don’t have a spine in moments like this.
**And that’s the problem, Peter.**
Too many Democrats don’t get that this moment demands urgency. Demands boldness. Demands a new generation of leaders who won’t roll over when it matters most.
That’s exactly what Leaders We Deserve is about:
→ Finding young progressives (the next Robert Garcia)
→ Getting them elected and into leadership roles
→ Giving them the resources to _actually fight_
But we can’t do this without grassroots support from people like you.
**[Can you pitch in $5 or anything you can now to help us keep up the fight?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20251113_1_epstein.N6SXmK&refcode=em20251113-2833&amount=5&t=3&akid=2833%2E587540%2EtIiweJ)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20251113_1_epstein.N6SXmK&amount=5&refcode=em20251113-2833&t=22&akid=2833%2E587540%2EtIiweJ)**
We all deserve a Democratic Party that doesn’t back down — and that starts with changing who we elect, embracing a culture of weeding out the feckless folders we have in this party in our safe seats via primaries, and winning majorities that have the spine to actually use their power to hold Trump's feet to the fire and NOT cave in moments like what we just saw.
Thanks for being in this fight with us.
— David Hogg

He’s been demanding answers, standing up to Republicans, and now — finally — we’re seeing action. Just yesterday Rep. Adelita Grijalva was sworn in despite Speaker Mike Johnson’s attempts to delay her. Her first move? Signing the discharge petition to release the Epstein files. That means we’re just a week away from real accountability: who Epstein trafficked kids to, and who in power helped cover it up. Compare that with the eight Senate Democrats (nearly all of whom are retiring) who just caved on the government shutdown, handing a victory to Republicans instead of continuing to fight. If anyone should have been worried about the vulnerability of their seat and voted with Republicans, it should have been someone like Ossoff in Georgia or Gallego in Arizona (both younger senators), but they still did not vote to cave to the Republicans and who did? Eight Senators who have been there for decades and have all the experience in the world, but none of the courage to make it matter. Experience matters, but it means NOTHING if you don’t have a spine in moments like this. And that’s the problem, Peter. Too many Democrats don’t get that this moment demands urgency. Demands boldness. Demands a new generation of leaders who won’t roll over when it matters most. That’s exactly what Leaders We Deserve is about: → Finding young progressives (the next Robert Garcia) → Getting them elected and into leadership roles → Giving them the resources to actually fight But we can’t do this without grassroots support from people like you. We all deserve a Democratic Party that doesn’t back down — and that starts with changing who we elect, embracing a culture of weeding out the feckless folders we have in this party in our safe seats via primaries, and winning majorities that have the spine to actually use their power to hold Trump's feet to the fire and NOT cave in moments like what we just saw. Thanks for being in this fight with us. — David Hogg

| | Dorian Gray glanced at the picture, and suddenly an uncontrollable feeling of hatred for Basil Hallward came over him, as though it had been suggested to him by the image on the canvas, whispered into his ear by those grinning lips. The mad passions of a hunted animal stirred within him, and he loathed the man who was seated at the table, more than in his whole life he had ever loathed anything. He glanced wildly around. Something glimmered on the top of the painted chest that faced him. His eye fell on it. He knew what it was. It was a knife that he had brought up, some days before, to cut a piece of cord, and had forgotten to take away with him. He moved slowly towards it, passing Hallward as he did so. As soon as he got behind him, he seized it and turned round. Hallward stirred in his chair as if he was going to rise. He rushed at him and dug the knife into the great vein that is behind the ear, crushing the man’s head down on the table and stabbing again and again. There was a stifled groan and the horrible sound of some one choking with blood. Three times the outstretched arms shot up convulsively, waving grotesque, stiff-fingered hands in the air. He stabbed him twice more, but the man did not move. Something began to trickle on the floor. He waited for a moment, still pressing the head down. Then he threw the knife on the table, and listened. He could hear nothing, but the drip, drip on the threadbare carpet. He opened the door and went out on the landing. The house was absolutely quiet. No one was about. For a few seconds he stood bending over the balustrade and peering down into the black seething well of darkness. Then he took out the key and returned to the room, locking himself in as he did so. The thing was still seated in the chair, straining over the table with bowed head, and humped back, and long fantastic arms. Had it not been for the red jagged tear in the neck and the clotted black pool that was slowly widening on the table, one would have said that the man was simply asleep. How quickly it had all been done! He felt strangely calm, and walking over to the window, opened it and stepped out on the balcony. The wind had blown the fog away, and the sky was like a monstrous peacock’s tail, starred with myriads of golden eyes. He looked down and saw the policeman going his rounds and flashing the long beam of his lantern on the doors of the silent houses. The crimson spot of a prowling hansom gleamed at the corner and then vanished. A woman in a fluttering shawl was creeping slowly by the railings, staggering as she went. Now and then she stopped and peered back. Once, she began to sing in a hoarse voice. The policeman strolled over and said something to her. She stumbled away, laughing. A bitter blast swept across the square. The gas-lamps flickered and became blue, and the leafless trees shook their black iron branches to and fro. He shivered and went back, closing the window behind him.

Ivan Dmytrovych Sirko was born in the early seventeenth century, approximately between 1605 and 1610. This is evidenced primarily by the results of research on Sirko's remains, according to which the Cossack ataman was 70-75 years old at the time of his death in 1680. The first researcher of Sirko's biography, the famous Ukrainian historian Dmytro Yavornytskyi, suggested that the future ataman was born in Sloboda Ukraine in the settlement of Merefa (now the city of Merefa, Kharkiv region). However, this is not true. Merefa was founded only in 1658, i.e. when Sirko was in his late teens. However, Sirko and his family lived in Merefa for a long time in his house, and after his death, his wife and some family members lived there. The fact that Merefa in Slobozhanshchyna is associated with the name of the Cossack Ataman is evidenced by another name for the town recorded in some Ukrainian chronicles, Sirkivka. Where, then, should we look for Sirko's homeland? In our opinion, the sources give grounds to localize it in Eastern Podillia, namely in the Vinnytsia region. It is worth recalling that Sirko was a colonel in Vinnytsia (Kalnytsia) in 1658-1660. As you know, at that time in Ukraine, people who came from the local area were usually elected to such positions. Let us also recall a letter from Hetman of the Left Bank Ukraine Ivan Samoilovych to the tsarist voivode Prince G. Romodanovsky of April 20, 1675*, which recounts (in Russian) Sirko's own words: "And since I was born among the Poles, I want to die there." Thus, it is clear that Sirko was born on the Ukrainian lands that were under the rule of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, not Muscovy (the latter included Slobozhanshchyna). The historian Volodymyr Borysenko's assumption that Sirko's birthplace was the hundred-man town of the Bratslav regiment Murafa, a few kilometers from Kalnyk, is correct. Now it is the village of Zhdanov, Vinnytsia region. By the way, Murafa in the Slobozhanshchyna probably originated from this Murafa, because immigrants from the Right Bank of Ukraine to the Left Bank often gave the newly founded settlements the names of their native villages or towns. It is also worth noting Sirko's great interest in Keleberda, which he founded in 1675 on the left bank of the Dnipro. For a long time, he sought from the Moscow tsar the right to own this town or sloboda, as well as the strategically important crossing of the Dnipro near Perevolochna (Sirko wanted this crossing not for himself, but for the entire Zaporozhian Lowland Army). Contrary to popular belief, we believe that Sirko did not come from a Cossack family, but from a small Ukrainian Orthodox gentry. For example, we know the name of a Podillia nobleman, Voytekh Sirko, who was married to a certain Olena Kozynska. Sources mention them in 1592. ICYMI, a small group of Democrats broke ranks and agreed to the GOP’s disastrous bill without any promise to protect our health care.
It’s an insult to hard-working families in Oregon and across the country just trying to get by. It’s a sellout.

## The Numbers Tell a Clear Story
The Axios-Telemundo-Ipsos polling series, conducted periodically since December 2021, reveals a striking consistency: **51% of Latinos say inflation and cost of living is their top priority.** Not immigration. Not social issues. The economy.
Immigration has risen to second place at 29%, but let that sink in--there's a 20-point gap between the top concern and the runner-up. As Russell put it perfectly: "The economy affects 100% of us. When it's bad, every Latino in the country is affected by it."
## The Immigration Complexity
Yes, immigration matters. It's moved up from fourth or fifth place to second, jumping from about 21% in June 2022 to 29% today. But here's the nuance that gets lost in mainstream coverage: Latinos are concerned about immigration for the same reasons as other Americans--they're alarmed by images of ICE raids in preschools, by questions of due process, by the chaos they're seeing unfold.
This isn't just about personal impact. It's about values, fairness, and what kind of country we want to be. And crucially, many Latinos also connect immigration enforcement to economic concerns--who's going to pick the crops? Why did my tree removal cost double?
## Politically Unhoused
Perhaps the most striking finding: **Only 31% of Latinos now say it 's a good time to be Latino in America, down from 67% in June 2022.** That's not a shift--that's an earthquake.
Russell coined a phrase I'm stealing: Latinos are "politically unhoused." Nearly a quarter say neither party represents them. They view Republicans as problematic on race, but Democrats as condescending. When both parties fail you, you vote with your pocketbook.
And here's the kicker: Trump's favorability among Latinos sits at about 30%--roughly the same percentage who think it's a good time to be Latino in America. In just ten months, Trump has erased a decade of Republican gains with Latino voters through bad economic policy and chaotic governance.
## The Working-Class Coalition Nobody's Building
Russell and I explored something deeper: the potential for a blue-collar, working-class Latino political movement that transcends party lines. Not a resurrection of La Raza Unida, but a recognition that 75% of Latinos share a common identity--we're the essential workforce, the working class.
He pointed to historical examples: Robert Kennedy connecting Appalachia to the Mississippi Delta to Pine Ridge. Reverend Barber organizing poor whites and poor blacks in Kentucky to elect Andy Beshear. There's a model here, a template for bringing together the vaqueros, the jibaros, the ranch libertarians who distrust both the corrupt Mexican government and the racist American one.
But can such a leader emerge? Can they survive the primary gatekeepers of either party when they don't check the conventional boxes? When they say, "I care about climate change, but Juan needs that oil job that pays $120K, and you can't promise me a wind farm will employ him and all his cousins by Monday"?
## The American Dream Deferred
Only 44% of Latinos now believe they can live the American Dream, down from 61% in March 2022. That's a 17-point collapse in belief in the core promise of America.
This is the opening. This is the opportunity. But it requires something both parties seem incapable of: authentic engagement with working-class concerns, a real narrative about affordability and belonging, and the courage to challenge elite assumptions on both the left and right.
As Russell noted, Democrats offer ten-point plans while Republicans offer narratives. Trump said "no tax on tips" with zero evidence of implementation, but it resonated because it was simple, direct, and spoke to felt economic pain.
## The Path Forward
The data is clear. The science is settled. Latino voters are not a mystery--they're rational actors responding to economic conditions that are crushing them. They want secure borders AND a pathway to citizenship. They want good jobs AND respect for their values. They're not ideological; they're practical.
The question isn't what Latinos want. It's whether anyone in power is listening.

Trump said "no tax on tips" with zero evidence of implementation, but it resonated because it was simple, direct, and spoke to felt economic pain. The Path Forward The data is clear. The science is settled. Latino voters are not a mystery--they're rational actors responding to economic conditions that are crushing them. They want secure borders AND a pathway to citizenship. They want good jobs AND respect for their values. They're not ideological; they're practical. The question isn't what Latinos want. It's whether anyone in power is listening. *Out on Substack first! Give us a heart & share this post if you think more people need to understand what Latino voters actually care about. The Latino Vote Podcast is free today. | | Dear Peter,
---
California’s redwoods have stood tall for thousands of years. They’ve weathered storms, fires, and time itself. But today, they face challenges unlike any before: megafires, drought, and weakened protections for our public lands and wildlife.
---
That’s why we created the **[Redwood Resilience Fund](https://click.everyaction.com/k/119236081/582387276/1781219864?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9TVFJXTC9TVFJXTC8xLzg5NTc0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjk0Yjc1NGU4LWUwYzAtZjAxMS04MTk2LTYwNDViZGZlOGU5YyIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=j-ptr-oUUrB6PB5k0vzkItI8CXbXv8b2ES3eI5VXdKk=&emci=45831135-53bf-f011-8194-00224823ff9b&emdi=94b754e8-e0c0-f011-8196-6045bdfe8e9c&ceid=1504551)**. It’s a bold new initiative to help forests—and the people and communities that depend on them—adapt and thrive far into the future. In a time of uncertainty, this fund provides something powerful and actionable we can do together.
---
With your support, we’ll advance key efforts across the redwood range, including: **• Climate Resilience** – We’ll keep protecting centuries-old coast redwoods as powerful carbon sinks, expanding restoration work at sites like Harold Richardson Redwoods Reserve to support a stable climate for generations to come. **• Wildfire Resilience** – We’re restoring giant sequoia groves across the Sierra, including at Alder Creek, where we’re removing fire fuels and supporting tribal-led cultural burns to protect giant sequoias from extreme fires. **• Park Resilience** – At Founders Grove in Humboldt Redwoods State Park, we’re developing plans to restore old-growth habitat, remove aging infrastructure, and create new trails and inclusive exhibits that welcome all visitors. **• Community Resilience** – We’ll deepen collaboration with communities and local partners to shape education, cultural programs, and public access across the entire redwood range. The challenges are substantial, but through the [**Redwood Resilience Fund** ,](https://click.everyaction.com/k/119236082/582387277/1781219864?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9TVFJXTC9TVFJXTC8xLzg5NTc0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjk0Yjc1NGU4LWUwYzAtZjAxMS04MTk2LTYwNDViZGZlOGU5YyIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=j-ptr-oUUrB6PB5k0vzkItI8CXbXv8b2ES3eI5VXdKk=&emci=45831135-53bf-f011-8194-00224823ff9b&emdi=94b754e8-e0c0-f011-8196-6045bdfe8e9c&ceid=1504551) so is our power to make a difference. When we act together, we can protect irreplaceable forests, boost climate resiliency, and strengthen our communities. The tomorrow we want? It begins by taking action today.
---

**_DEADLINE: 11:59PM TONIGHT_** **[JOIN THE FOCUS GROUP](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/97644?t=1&akid=9709%2E614464%2EtiKKhz)** After the big elections last week, which brought major victories for Democrats up + down the ballot all across the country, we want to check in: **Will you be part of our November 2025 Focus Group?** It takes less than 3 minutes. You can do it from your phone or your computer. name: Wesley Bell
subject: My vote last night
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY BELL FOR MISSOURI
body:
You should have the consequences made clear to you. Peter,

Washington's dysfunction has left us with the longest government shutdown in American history.

For 43 days, Mike Johnson and Donald Trump made it clear they'd do anything to get their way. They held our healthcare, wages, and even the food on our table hostage, all while the American people paid the price.

And to top it all off, the spending bill that passed last night was just another slap in the face from GOP leadership. **The budget does nothing for the 24 million Americans who will see their healthcare costs _double_ by the end of the year.**

I have to ask, Peter: Who is Mike Johnson working for? It sure isn't Louisiana. His state is expected to see the steepest decline in healthcare coverage in the nation, a 61% drop.

This budget will have lasting consequences in Louisiana, Missouri, and across the nation. It will devastate families who are already struggling to afford their healthcare and force countless families to go without coverage.

I'm telling you this not to scare you, but because you should have the consequences made clear to you. You need to know that I voted NO on the GOP's sham deal because I believe St. Louis deserves a representative who will show up for them, not Donald Trump, not the 1%, and certainly not for themselves.

**My first priority will always be to hear and raise the voices of the people in our community. I'm in this fight for you, and I'll keep fighting to cut costs and bring our hard-earned dollars back to our district.**

In solidarity,

Whether you subscribed to my campaign website a week ago, or all the way back in spring of 2024, I want to thank you for being a part of our effort to flip the 6th congressional district blue. In case you missed the update from my campaign social media, I’m excited to let you know that I’m back in the fight for the 2026 midterms. From the cost of living to supporting our region’s farmers to restoring access to folks’ healthcare, there’s a lot of work to be done. I said it in 2024, and it’s more true than ever now: we need a representative who will leave no one behind. Now is the time to bring real change to the 6th district, the Commonwealth, and the country as a whole. That’s why I hope you’ll join me tomorrow for my campaign kickoff: WHERE: Harrisonburg Courthouse ADDRESS: 80 Court Square, Harrisonburg, VA 22802 WHEN: 1:30 PM And join me afterwards at the Golden Pony restaurant just a couple blocks north of the Courthouse from 2:00-4:00 PM for a celebration. Peter, I’m grateful for your support. It’ll take a lot to flip this seat, but I know that together we can deliver for the 6th district. Yours, Ken | Ken Mitchell for Virginia, PO Box 1795, Harrisonburg, VA 22803, USA Powered by

# **Trump Administration designates four European Antifa groups as terrorist organizations**
The State Department announced Thursday it will classify four violent far-left organizations operating in Germany, Italy and Greece as **[foreign terrorist organizations.](https://substack.com/redirect/5b032fc4-11a5-43d0-bffb-2829d91f6e11?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

---|---|---
* **Groups targeted** : Antifa Ost, the International Revolutionary Front, Armed Proletarian Justice, and Revolutionary Class Self Defense were identified for "using force against those they identify as opponents of their Marxist and anarchist projects."
* **Recent violence** : Germany-based Antifa Ost participated in a 2023 counter-demonstration against neo-Nazis in Budapest, with German Interior Ministry reports warning the group shows no signs of stopping. In Italy, the International Revolutionary Front kneecapped a nuclear engineering executive in 2012, while Greece's Revolutionary Class Self Defense bombed the Greek Ministry of Labor and Hellenic Railway, dedicating attacks to "the Palestinian people and their heroic resistance."
* **Financial consequences** : The classification blocks the groups from accessing the U.S. financial system and enables prosecution of anyone providing support. State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott said "the anarchists, Marxists, and violent extremists of Antifa have waged a terror campaign in the United States and across the Western world for decades..."
* **Domestic context** : President Trump declared Antifa a "major" terrorist organization on Sept. 17, six days after conservative activist Charlie Kirk's assassination. A subsequent executive order directed all federal agencies to investigate and dismantle illegal Antifa operations and prosecute those funding such activities.

# **Sen. John hospitalized following heart-related fall near Pennsylvania home**
Sen. John Fetterman, D-Pa., was **[admitted to a hospital](https://substack.com/redirect/de90a9ae-ff5e-4ff8-86eb-2e94165d4c8b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** Thursday after falling near his Braddock, Pennsylvania.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f5199cd9-6873-4ca4-b869-6c3221b37baa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **What happened** : Fetterman was taken to a Pittsburgh medical facility for precautionary evaluation after the incident, which resulted in facial injuries described as minor. Medical personnel discovered a ventricular fibrillation episode led to his lightheadedness before he collapsed and struck his face. The senator quipped about the situation, stating "If you thought my face looked bad before, wait until you see it now!"
* **Medical status** : Fetterman is "doing well" as he continues to be observed at the hospital. The spokesperson noted he opted to stay for monitoring while doctors recalibrate his medication following the cardiac event.
* **Previous ailments** : The Pennsylvania lawmaker has confronted medical challenges previously, particularly a serious stroke that affected him during his 2022 Senate race. Fetterman recently garnered attention for diverging from fellow Democrats throughout the government shutdown by supporting measures to restore federal operations.

# **Assailant targets acting NJ U.S. Attorney Alina Habba**
Attorney General Pam Bondi revealed Thursday that **[someone accosted Acting U.S. Attorney](https://substack.com/redirect/fe6c9c0d-9561-4bd2-8bea-97d096c9ff0e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** for the District of New Jersey Alina Habba on Wednesday evening, smashing items in her workplace before law enforcement could respond.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/fe6c9c0d-9561-4bd2-8bea-97d096c9ff0e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Bondi 's warning**: The attorney general said Habba was not injured but characterized the episode as part of a growing trend of radicals assaulting law enforcement personnel across America. "Any violence or threats of violence against any federal officer will not be tolerated. Period," Bondi declared, promising investigators would track down the culprit and pursue maximum charges.
* **Habba defiant** : After the assault, the acting U.S. attorney said she refuses to be intimidated from performing her responsibilities. "I will not be intimidated by radical lunatics for doing my job," Habba said. Habba manages all federal criminal cases and civil lawsuits where the government has stakes in New Jersey, leading roughly 155 federal prosecutors and 130 administrative staff throughout facilities in Newark, Camden and Trenton.
* **Ongoing investigation** : Authorities have not released further specifics about the confrontation as they pursue leads to capture and charge the individual. The Justice Department promised to "use every legal tool available" to protect federal personnel and hold violent criminals fully responsible.

* * *
# **DHS secretary hands out $10,000 bonuses to TSA agents who worked during shutdown**
Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem gave**[$10,000 bonus checks](https://substack.com/redirect/a9d7b64b-7023-4d11-8294-4c793f5ae72b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** Thursday to Transportation Security Administration workers who stayed on duty during the 43-day government closure at Houston's George Bush Intercontinental Airport.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/32b33899-87f6-40fe-ac9b-4715b6524cd5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* **Bonus distribution** : Noem handed checks directly to roughly 20 agents and said all TSA staff who reported for work throughout the shutdown would receive payment to assist with financial recovery.

name: Deb Haaland
subject: If Trump gets away with this, the damage will be irreversible
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR AND AUTHORIZED BY DEB FOR NEW MEXICO
body:
Trump is considering destroying Chaco Canyon. We must act now.
# [](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/133?t=1&akid=5670%2E400544%2ESrScPo)
This is urgent.
**The Trump Administration just took the first step towards reopening sacred public lands around Chaco Canyon to oil and gas drilling.**
Right now, they’re considering revoking the 20-year drilling ban that community leaders fought hard to secure. _That protection could now be rolled back — or completely erased._
**[We cannot let this happen. Please add your name to oppose the destruction of Chaco Canyon and protect our public lands from Donald Trump.](https://act.debhaaland.com/signup/protect-chaco-canyon/?source=em20251113-5670&t=2&akid=5670%2E400544%2ESrScPo)**
**[Add Your Name »](https://act.debhaaland.com/signup/protect-chaco-canyon/?source=em20251113-5670&t=3&akid=5670%2E400544%2ESrScPo)**
Let’s be clear: This is about protecting identity, ancestry, and our obligation to honor sacred public lands.
For generations, Pueblo and Tribal communities have prayed, gathered, and walked the paths of Chaco. These lands hold stories written in stone.
**As Secretary of the Interior, I worked to protect Chaco and ban new drilling within 10 miles of the site for 20 years — a victory shaped by community voices. Now, Trump is threatening to unravel everything we fought for.**
If he gets away with this, it could open hundreds of square miles of land to drilling in New Mexico. That would do irreversible damage to the landscape, poison our water, and desecrate sites tied to the spiritual and cultural foundations of our state’s ancestors.
**[Chaco is not for sale. Will you please join me and add your name to say NO drilling in Chaco Canyon?](https://act.debhaaland.com/signup/protect-chaco-canyon/?source=em20251113-5670&t=4&akid=5670%2E400544%2ESrScPo)**
**[Add Your Name »](https://act.debhaaland.com/signup/protect-chaco-canyon/?source=em20251113-5670&t=5&akid=5670%2E400544%2ESrScPo)**
Thank you for speaking up today,
Deb

body:

I'm running to represent NY-12 in Congress! This is the district where I was born and raised, and the place that five generations of my family have called home.

Hi friend, I'm Jack Schlossberg, and my grandfather, President Kennedy, is my hero.

In high school, I spent hours watching his speeches. He taught us all that politics isn't about serving yourself — it's about serving others. And that's exactly why I'm running for Congress.

[**This isn't going to be your average campaign — we’re at the forefront of a movement backed by real people who are ready for a new generation of leadership. I won't be bought or intimidated. Instead, I'll be relying on folks like you. So, if you're willing to be one of the first donors to my campaign, will you split a donation between myself and the Voter Protection Project right now? »**](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/96563?t=7&akid=21850%2E878179%2EGOkWVT) If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your split donation between Jack Schlossberg and VPP will go through immediately: | [CONTRIBUTE $10 »](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/96564?t=8&akid=21850%2E878179%2EGOkWVT)

I've always been passionate about politics — you can probably gather as much if you've seen any of my social media posts :) I pride myself on my hot (correct!) takes. But public service has always been my driving force. I come from a long legacy of public service, from my great-great-grandparents to my mother, Caroline Kennedy.

**I have big shoes to fill. I've known it all my life.** But this is even bigger than living up to my family name. This is about serving the people of New York — the city that shaped me into the person I am today.

subject: We Deserve Better

body:
ELIZABETH PANNILL FLETCHER FOR CONGRESS [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP10/1/82676/images/Non-Re-Elect%20Logo.png]
Yesterday, Speaker Johnson called the House of Representatives back after 55 days. It wasn’t my first time back in Washington. I have been coming back, as have my colleagues in the House Democratic Caucus, ready to work on and negotiate a bill to reopen the government and to address the real challenges facing Americans, especially the growing health care crisis this Congress has created.
But that is not the bill the House considered. It could have been. And it should have been. Instead—after insisting that nothing could be done other than the Senate passing the prior House bill—House Republicans presented the bill the Senate passed with no House input and no amendments, one that ignores the health care crisis and includes obscene million-dollar payouts to eight Republican Senators.
Throughout the long government shutdown, we asked Speaker Johnson to meet with us, to negotiate with Democrats, to find common ground on keeping open, and later reopening, the government. For weeks, communities across the United States endured the consequences of the government shutdown.
Even though the House Republicans have been on vacation since September 19, yesterday they claimed that ending the government shutdown was so urgent that all they could do was pass the Senate bill. It is, of course, a false claim and a false choice. But I supposed it was not really a surprise.
I sponsored amendments to the bill to strike the obscene million-dollar payouts to Republican Senators, to extend Affordable Care Act premium tax credits, and to protect SNAP benefits during funding lapses. House Republicans could easily have adopted them, could have done something to address these glaring failures. But, this do-nothing House could not be bothered.
And that is why they should not be in charge of the House. House Republicans have demonstrated not only that they cannot govern, but that they have no interest in doing it. What are they interested in now? Blaming Democrats and hiding the Epstein files.
Texans—and all Americans—deserve better.
I will keep fighting for a responsible, transparent, and accountable government that works for the people of TX07 and people across the country. Taking back the House majority—the work of this campaign—is critical to that effort. So, thanks for all you continue to do to make that possible.
Together we can do anything,

You ever have one of those shows that hits like a live wire? That this one. David Shuster and I were already revved up--Epstein's emails had just dropped, exposing not just Trump's grotesque proximity to that predator, but the rot in a media machine too timid to tell the truth. Then we brought in Egberto Willies, and the voltage went through the roof.
I'll say it again: the emails prove Trump wasn't some distant acquaintance of Jeffrey Epstein. He was _in it._ He's mentioned everywhere--in the victims' accounts, in Epstein's own words, even as the monster calls Trump "the worst human being alive." Yet our so-called mainstream media gives us graphics like "Epstein Mentions Trump Several Times." Several? Try thousands. Watch Shuster's full breakdown in **[Trump Knew: Epstein Emails Expose His Lies](https://substack.com/redirect/e3f003c8-4414-4137-b132-7a0abc768b9c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**.

* * *
That's what drives us mad--the lack of courage to speak plainly. _**The New York Times**_ and the networks act like context is a four-letter word. They wring their hands about "bias" while the Supreme Court, stacked with Federalist Society drones, shreds the Constitution and waves away crimes as "immunity." These aren't judges; they're political operatives in robes.
Egberto came in like a force of nature. He reminded us that when the judiciary is corrupt, you don't hide the evidence--you throw it all out there for the people to see. He's right. If the courts won't defend democracy, citizens have to. That's why independent media matters. That's why we built _Blue Amp Media_.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5cfa314e-5323-430f-8f3d-508f1f8ad59d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Egberto also cut right to the bone: "Certain lives matter, certain lives don't--that's always been U.S. policy." From Panama to Palestine, from Venezuela to our own borders, Trump's regime--and now his enablers--carry out cruelty as policy. And the media looks away unless it sells clicks. When the president literally bombs civilians in international waters, they shrug.
But give them a sex scandal, and suddenly it's wall-to-wall coverage.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/3ee2b575-bb5d-4265-9a0f-9b1e4cfe56bf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
It's all connected. Whether it's Trump's White House asbestos pit of corruption (**[that story's here](https://substack.com/redirect/e7f610b5-2ea2-464b-97ca-702343f29891?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**), or the Epstein files, or the emoluments, or the immunity scam--the disease is the same: unaccountable power, rotted institutions, and a press too scared to fight back.
But here's the good news: we are. Egberto's _[Politics Done Right](https://substack.com/redirect/02fadfdb-0875-4035-ab9d-723a2c11f406?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_ is growing out of Houston. David's fearless reporting keeps setting the bar higher. And _Blue Amp Media_? We're not waiting for gatekeepers to bless us--we're building the gate. With every show, every article, every subscriber, we're proving that truth still draws a crowd.
And there's hope, because even inside the Democratic Party, people are waking up. Chris Murphy is calling out Schumer's failures. Tammy Duckworth, Ro Khanna--they're standing up instead of bowing down. As Egberto said, "It takes a lot to build something--but together, we can." Damn right.
So if you're reading this, if you've made it this far, here's the ask: don't just nod along. Share this. Tell your friends that independent media is how we fight fascism and how we rebuild a democratic culture that deserves the name.
Because the empire of lies only wins if we stop flooding the zone with truth.

Peter,

It's official: the House finished the job last night and reopened the government **without** protecting ACA tax credits for millions of Americans. Six Democrats flipped to vote with Republicans. Six. Marie Glusenkamp-Perez will come as no shock. Every one of those six Democrats needs to go. Every one of them who gave up and rolled over, allowing Republicans to spike the cost of premiums - doubling them in some cases for millions of low and middle-income Americans. That's not just an inconvenience: it's life or death. It means you don't get your routine check-ups, and your cancer isn't caught early. It means you don't call an ambulance, even though you know you should. It means you never learn your blood pressure is high, and you need medication. Democrats refused to sign the Republicans' so-called "Clean CR" weeks ago for one reason: to protect the ACA. subject: ICE stormed a *daycare*

body:
A teacher was just violently arrested by ICE in front of her students.
# [](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20251113-5623-footer&t=1&akid=5623%2E420207%2EMLNlVY)
What happened last week in Chicago should outrage all of us, Peter.
ICE violently detained a beloved teacher just as school was starting for the day. Armed agents with guns and masks showed up with no warrant, slammed her to the ground, and dragged her away in front of crying children and terrified families.
[](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-email-20251113-1.SH_6_m&refcode=em20251113-5623&amount=3&t=2&akid=5623%2E420207%2EMLNlVY)
The woman arrested _has a work permit._ They took her anyway.
**This is what happens when ICE is allowed to operate with zero accountability, oversight, or human decency.**
And it’s why I’ve done everything from introducing legislation to rein in their power, holding hearings and demanding answers, and calling this agency exactly what it is: dangerous and unchecked.
But here’s the truth: as long as MAGA Republicans have power in Congress, the cruelty will continue. More due process will be denied, more Black and Brown communities will be targeted, and more immigrant families will be terrorized — including in their schools.
We’re less than a year out from the midterms, and what we do right now decides everything. We can organize, flip the House, and _finally_ start holding this administration accountable — or face two more years of unchecked, escalating abuse.
[**If you’re ready to fight back, will you chip in today to help us win back the House and stop the MAGA cruelty agenda at the source?**](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-email-20251113-1.SH_6_m&refcode=em20251113-5623&amount=3&t=3&akid=5623%2E420207%2EMLNlVY)
**[Contribute $3](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-email-20251113-1.SH_6_m&amount=3&refcode=em20251113-5623&t=22&akid=5623%2E420207%2EMLNlVY)**
This fight is deeply personal for me. I’ve spent my life organizing and fighting for immigrant rights. I know how much pain these policies inflict. And I also know that we cannot stop fighting back, supporting immigrant communities, or start acting like this is normal.
Thank you for standing up.
Pramila Jayapal
**[Contribute](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/pj-email-footer?refcode=em20251113-5623-footer&t=23&refcode2=5623_420207_MLNlVY&akid=5623%2E420207%2EMLNlVY)**
